title: feat(approvals): an escalation deadline can count working time on an org calendar (clock: working_time)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D62xGLMbyWJaMEVnAMEjTK1)_
Fixes #35357
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up #35931 — skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md (the escalation row), domain:skills sub-card, Blocked-by this PR

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：审批节点的超时升级可以选择「按工作时间计算」，按组织的工作日历跳过夜间、周末和节假日，并计入调休补班日；日历算不出时，审批收件箱在到期时间处显示「日历算不出」和原因。
- 为什么做：工作日历分期的第四张卡，让审批超时和工作日历一起发布，周五下午提交的审批不再在周五晚上就升级。
- 出错会怎样：只影响选了「工作时间」的审批节点；默认仍按自然小时，已在途的审批到期时间不变，可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

ADR-0157 D5, D9 and D12, on the approval escalation:

- **Spec** (`ApprovalEscalationSchema`): two optional keys. `clock: 'wall_clock' | 'working_time'`, default `'wall_clock'` (a stored snapshot carries no `clock`, so every open request keeps its deadline), and `calendar`, a working-calendar code (`WORK_CALENDAR_CODE_PATTERN`). The `timeoutHours` describe text and comment no longer say the platform ships no calendar; they say the clock decides how the hours count. The describe first sentences stay in business words.
- **Runtime** (`plugin-approvals`): one deadline function, `ApprovalService.slaDeadline`, serves both the escalation sweep and the request read projection (D12). `wall_clock` is the unchanged `slaDueAt` (`created_at + timeoutHours` elapsed). `working_time` counts `timeoutHours` working hours from `created_at` through the calendar service (`WORK_CALENDAR_SERVICE`, resolved lazily like the other providers), naming the request's own `organization_id` and `escalation.calendar`; the service resolves the named code, else the organization default, else refuses. It is recomputed on every sweep and every read, never stored. `slaDueAt` answers nothing for a `working_time` escalation, so no path can fall back to wall-clock hours (D2). Single-shot escalation (ADR-0042 §1) is untouched: the `escalate` audit row is still the only marker, and it does not record the due time.
- **Cannot answer** (D9): a calendar refusal (`ERR_WORK_CALENDAR_UNRESOLVED`, `ERR_WORK_CALENDAR_NOT_MAINTAINED`, `ERR_WORK_CALENDAR_INVALID`) is not an escalation: the sweep skips the request, counts it in one `warn` per sweep, and asks again next sweep. A kernel with no calendar service refuses the same way. **New served field (additive): `sla_due_refusal`** on `ApprovalRequestRow` (`code`, `reason` on unresolved, `calendar`, `date` on not-maintained, `message`), present in place of `sla_due_at`.
- **Lint** (`@objectstack/lint`): `approval-escalation-calendar-without-working-time` (error) refuses a `calendar` beside the wall clock, where nothing reads it. Static only: no check that the calendar exists (D9).
- **Studio**: the approval inspector's escalation block gains "Count hours as" (wall-clock / working hours) and "Working calendar", which shows only under working time, from both descriptor sources (`SIBLING_GATES` in `json-schema-to-fields.ts` serves the hand-written table and the engine-published `configSchema`). zh overlay added; the `timeoutHours` zh help no longer says there is no calendar.
- **Console inbox**: where the SLA countdown sits, a pending row with `sla_due_refusal` shows "Calendar can't compute" with the reason (no calendar "X" / no default calendar / not maintained for DATE / fix the calendar in Setup), in all eleven locale packs (zh-Hans: 「日历算不出」).
- **Docs**: `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` (Timeouts and escalation) and the generated reference page. ADR anchor for the deadline function.

Not released alone: ships in the same release as the calendar objects and service (#35355) and the working-day formula functions (#35356), ADR-0157 D4.

## Evals

None: no agent-facing prompt or skill text changes here. The skills text is owed as a follow-up (the `Skills-docs:` line).

## Tests

- `approval-service-sla-calendar-clock.test.ts`, a new top-level describe on the REAL `WorkCalendarService` over a read double: Friday 17:00 + 4 working hours with Monday a holiday fires Tuesday 12:00 and not at any earlier instant; before a make-up (调休) Saturday it fires that Saturday 12:00; a holiday entered later moves the deadline (D12); a missing calendar serves `sla_due_refusal` (`not_found`), escalates nothing past every deadline, and the next sweep escalates once the calendar exists; `no_default` and `ERR_WORK_CALENDAR_NOT_MAINTAINED` (with its date); no calendar service refuses; an explicit `wall_clock` equals the default. The four existing wall-clock pins are unchanged and green.
- Lint: the finding fires on a calendar with no clock and with `wall_clock`; its control (`working_time` with a calendar that does not exist, and `working_time` with none) is clean.
- Inspector: the calendar is hidden on the default and an explicit wall clock, shown under working time, and a typed code round-trips through `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema`, from both descriptor sources. Inbox: the reason renders in place of the countdown in English and zh-CN, and a served due time keeps its countdown.
- Re-measured pins: the inspector's gated-field census 33 → 35, the declared-default surface ten → eleven (`escalation.clock`), and the escalation round-trip now parses with `clock: 'wall_clock'` materialized.

<details><summary>Ablations (both red, both restored to HEAD by `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`)</summary>

- Working-time branch (`slaDeadline` answers wall-clock for every clock): 6 of 12 tests red, the six `working_time` cases; restore blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Cannot-answer guard (a refusal no longer `continue`s the sweep): 3 of 12 red, each `expected { scanned: 1, escalated: 1 } to match object { escalated: +0 }`; restored to HEAD. A first attempt whose replacement was a substring of its anchor was refused by the tool before running and is not counted.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The served shape is additive: `sla_due_refusal` is new and optional; `sla_due_at` keeps its meaning under `wall_clock`.
- The `escalate` audit row does not record the due time it fired on (the ADR left this to this card); the deadline is never stored anywhere.
- A refused deadline is read once per row per read and sweep through the service's 60-second cache; reads of decided requests compute it too, so the projection stays one function for every status.
- The inbox reason is localized from the refusal's code; the server's English `message` is served but not shown.
- Not merged with `origin/main` (7 commits ahead at push time, none in the packages this diff touches); `overlap-check` reports clean merges against `origin/main`, #35789 and the two open locale-pack PRs.
